arxiv-2102-11744.title: Size effects and beyond-Fourier heat conduction in room-temperature experiments
arxiv-2102-11744.creator: A. Fehér 1 , N. Lukács 1 , L. Somlai 1,2 , T. Fodor 1 , M. Szücs 13 , T. Fülöp 13 , P. Ván 213 , R. Kovács 123
arxiv-2102-11744.description: Abstract . It is a long-lasting task to understand heat conduction phenomena beyond Fourier. Besides the low-temperature experiments on extremely pure crystals, it has turned out recently that heterogeneous materials with macro-scale size can also show thermal effects that cannot be modelled by the Fourier equation.

arxiv-2103-16560.title: Weak-Strong Uniqueness for the Isentropic Euler Equations with Possible Vacuum
arxiv-2103-16560.creator: Shyam Sundar Ghoshal, Animesh Jana, Emil Wiedemann
arxiv-2103-16560.description: Abstract We establish a weak-strong uniqueness result for the isentropic compressible Euler equations, that is: As long as a sufficiently regular solution exists, all energy-admissible weak solutions with the same initial data coincide with it. The main novelty in this contribution, compared to previous literature, is that we allow for possible vacuum in the strong solution.

arxiv-2210-01567.title: Extension bases in Henselian valued fields Thanks: The author was partially supported by GeoMod AAPG2019 (ANR-DFG), Geometric and Combinatorial Configurations in Model Theory.
arxiv-2210-01567.creator: Akash HOSSAIN
arxiv-2210-01567.description: Abstract . We study the behaviour of forking in valued fields, and we give several sufficient conditions for parameter sets in a Henselian valued field of residue characteristic zero to be an extension base. Notably, we consider arbitrary (potentially imaginary) bases, whereas previous related results in the literature only focus on maximally complete sets of parameters.

arxiv-2210-07055.title: Sparse in Space and Time: Audio-visual Synchronisation with Trainable Selectors
arxiv-2210-07055.creator: Vladimir Iashin, Weidi Xie, Esa Rahtu, Andrew Zisserman
arxiv-2210-07055.description: Abstract The objective of this paper is audio-visual synchronisation of general videos ‘in the wild’. For such videos, the events that may be harnessed for synchronisation cues may be spatially small and may occur only infrequently during a many seconds-long video clip, i.e the synchronisation signal is ‘sparse in space and time’.

arxiv-2304-05280.title: Typical X-ray Outburst Light Curves of Aql X-1 Accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal (ApJ)
arxiv-2304-05280.creator: Ömer Faruk Çoban, Ünal Ertan
arxiv-2304-05280.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Ömer Faruk Çoban, Ünal Ertan. We show that a typical X-ray outburst light curve of Aql X-1 can be reproduced by accretion onto the neutron star in the frame of the disk instability model without invoking partial accretion or propeller effect.

Piechocki \affilnum 4, Colin Robbins \affilnum 5,
arxiv-2312-14687.description: Abstract The way we travel is changing rapidly, and Cooperative Intelligent Transportation Systems (C-ITSs) are at the forefront of this evolution. However, the adoption of C-ITSs introduces new risks and challenges, making cybersecurity a top priority for ensuring safety and reliability.

arxiv-2504-06870.title: Bayesian Component Separation for DESI LAE Automated Spectroscopic Redshifts and Photometric Targeting Facilities: Mayall (DESI), Blanco (DECam)

Forero-Romero, Enrique Gaztañaga, Satya Gontc
arxiv-2504-06870.description: Abstract Lyman Alpha Emitters (LAEs) are valuable high-redshift cosmological probes traditionally identified using specialized narrow-band photometric surveys. In ground-based spectroscopy, it can be difficult to distinguish the sharp LAE peak from residual sky emission lines using automated methods, leading to misclassified redshifts.

arxiv-2506-06256.title: Quadratic Extended and Unscented Kalman Filter Updates Dr. Simone Servadio, Assistant Professor, Department of Aerospace Engineering, servadio@iastate.edu Mr. Chiran Cherian, Graduate Student, Department of Aerospace Engineering, cbckbc@iastate.edu
arxiv-2506-06256.creator: Simone Servadio, Chiran. B. Cherian
arxiv-2506-06256.description: Abstract Common filters are usually based on the linear approximation of the optimal minimum mean square error estimator. The Extended and Unscented Kalman Filters handle nonlinearity through linearization and unscented transformation, respectively, but remain linear estimators, meaning that the state estimate is a linear function of the measurement.

pmc-10660756.title: Maturity Offset, Anthropometric Characteristics and Vertical Force–Velocity Profile in Youth Basketball Players
pmc-10660756.creator: Pablo Jiménez-Daza, Luis Teba del Pino, Julio Calleja-Gonzalez, Eduardo Sáez de Villarreal, Roland Van den Tillaar
pmc-10660756.description: This work aimed to analyze the relationships between maturity offset, anthropometric variables and the vertical force–velocity profile in youth (12–18 years old) male basketball players. pmc-13074859.title: WEDGE-Net: Wavelet-Driven Memory-Efficient Anomaly Detection for Industrial Edge Computing
pmc-13074859.creator: Joon-Min Park, Gye-Young Kim
pmc-13074859.description: As deep learning-based Anomaly Detection (AD) transitions from theoretical research to industrial application, the focus is shifting towards operational efficiency and economic viability on edge devices. While recent studies have achieved remarkable detection accuracy on standard benchmarks, they often rely on heavy memory banks or complex backbones, which pose challenges for deployment in resource-constrained manufacturing environments.

pmc-13289479.title: Triple-valve replacement in repaired tetralogy of fallot patients with mirror-image dextrocardia: a case report
pmc-13289479.creator: Rui Lv, Deming Liu, Xiaona Lin, Juncheng Jiang, Chuanguo Xu, Hao Zhang, Bin Qiao
pmc-13289479.description: BackgroundThe co-occurrence of mirror-image dextrocardia and tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) is a rare congenital condition. Reoperative multivalve surgery in such patients, especially after repaired TOF, presents exceptional challenges due to the mirrored cardiac anatomy and altered surgical field. This case highlights the surgical strategy for concomitant tricuspid, mitral, and pulmonary valve replacement in this unique setting.

pmc-13447453.creator: Christoph Zindel, Sandro Hodel, Yichao Luo, Michel Meisterhans, Sandro F Fucentese, Lazaros Vlachopoulos
pmc-13447453.description: PurposeThe gold standard for the management of ruptured patellar tendon is the surgical repair with nonabsorbable sutures and additional reinforcement e.g. cerclage wires as described by McLaughlin in 1947. pmc-13507340.title: Psychosis as a multisystem disorder of aberrant aging
pmc-13507340.creator: Rachel Upthegrove, Amalie C M Couch, Antonio de Marvao, Benjamin I Perry, Fabiana Corsi-Zuelli, Jack Rogers, Lahiru Handunnetthi, Nicholas M Barnes, Nikolaos Koutsouleris, Paris A Lalousis, Toby Pillinger, Zachary Freyberg
pmc-13507340.description: Psychotic disorders, including schizophrenia and affective psychosis, affect ~3% of the population and typically emerge in early adulthood. Cardiometabolic disease accounts for much of the 20-year life-expectancy gap in psychosis. Evidence indicates potentially causal processes, often seen in aging, act within and beyond the brain, and before the onset of treatment; these include inflammation, metabolic and mitochondrial dysfunction.

pmc-13565692.title: Polycomb Group Proteins in Drosophila melanogaster
pmc-13565692.creator: Fei Gao, Zicheng Li, Xiaoping Yu, Sunjie Chen, Chengcheng Ye
pmc-13565692.description: Simple SummaryDuring development, cells must preserve their specific identities while continuously dividing and responding to environmental changes. This stability is maintained by epigenetic regulation, a system that controls gene activity without changing DNA sequences. Polycomb group (PcG) proteins are essential epigenetic regulators that form specialized protein complexes to maintain the silencing of key developmental genes and ensure stable cell identity.
